title: The Letter of Saint Alder's
premise: When Saint Alder's founding father, Ambrose Vane, is exhumed for a bicentennial reinterment, coroner Kestrel Coldharbour finds the coffin empty — and a second, newer body hidden beneath the false floor. As she investigates, Kestrel discovers that Vane's celebrated ledger of town benefactors is actually a coded record of debts, disappearances, and stolen identities maintained by successive town elders, and that her own late mother's name appears in it. The killer, town archivist Merrin Hale, has been erasing people who threatened to expose the ledger's living beneficiaries; the empty coffin was her message that no one in Saint Alder's history is who they claim. At the anniversary dinner, Kestrel publicly decodes the ledger, names Merrin, and chooses to stay in the town that lied to her — on the condition that it finally tells the truth.
about_author: Theo Joubert is the pen name of a former parish records clerk from coastal New England who spent a decade cataloguing gravestone inscriptions before turning to fiction. Their mysteries are known for quiet towns with loud secrets and protagonists who read cemeteries like ledgers.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Kestrel Coldharbour prepares Ambrose Vane's exhumation for the bicentennial reinterment, walking readers through her intimate knowledge of every grave in Saint Alder's. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: rootedness — she belongs here completely, or believes she does.

chapters.title: Empty Oak
chapters.summary: At the exhumation, the 180-year-old coffin holds no bones — only river stones and a folded modern photograph of the town square. The crowd gasps; the mayor demands discretion. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: vertigo, the ground itself proving untrustworthy.

chapters.title: What the Stones Kept
chapters.summary: Beneath the false floor, Kestrel finds a second compartment containing a recent corpse: unidentified, embalmed within the last decade. She quietly claims jurisdiction before the mayor can bury the discovery. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: grim resolve replacing shock.

chapters.title: The Benefactor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Researching Vane's famous ledger at the town archive, Kestrel notices columns that don't add up — payments to people who never appear elsewhere in records. Archivist Merrin Hale hovers, helpful and watchful. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: first unease about a person, not just a mystery.

chapters.title: A Face No One Missed
chapters.summary: The hidden body is identified as Tobias Wrenn, a drifter reported missing nine years ago whose case was closed as 'left town.' His sister arrives, furious and grieving. POV: alternating Kestrel and the sister, Ida Wrenn. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: Mother's Margins
chapters.summary: Sorting her late mother's papers, Kestrel finds an annotated copy of the ledger with a marginal note: 'Ask what happened to the Alder girls.' Her mother knew something. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: personal stakes ignite; the past reaches into her own house.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Committee
chapters.summary: Mayor Corliss pressures Kestrel to delay the investigation until after the anniversary dinner, framing it as civic loyalty. Old friends echo him. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: claustrophobia — belonging revealed as a leash.

chapters.title: Debts in Disguise
chapters.summary: Kestrel cracks the ledger's first cipher layer: entries pair missing persons with inheritances funneled to founding families. Three of the four founding surnames still sit on the town council. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: cold clarity; this is a machine, not an accident.

chapters.title: Ida's Road Map
chapters.summary: Ida shares Tobias's letters hinting he'd found 'the book that eats people.' Together they map six unsolved disappearances onto ledger dates. POV: Ida. Emotional beat: alliance forged from shared loss.

chapters.title: Night in the Archive
chapters.summary: Breaking into the archive after hours, Kestrel photographs the original ledger but triggers an alarm. Fleeing, she glimpses someone watching from the stacks. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: The fourth founding surname — Coldharbour — appears as ledger victims, not beneficiaries. Kestrel realizes her mother was investigating too, and died the same week her last entry was made. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: bereavement reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: Merrin's Kindness
chapters.summary: Merrin offers Kestrel tea, sympathy, and a plausible theory blaming the mayor. It almost works — until Kestrel notices Merrin's gloves hide paper cuts matching the ledger's brittle pages. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: betrayal dawning slowly, painfully.

chapters.title: The Alder Girls
chapters.summary: Digging into the 1890s, Kestrel learns two sisters vanished after accusing Vane's heirs of forgery; one survived under a new name — possibly Kestrel's ancestor. Identity itself becomes the crime scene. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: uncanny recognition across generations.

chapters.title: Corliss Confesses (Partly)
chapters.summary: Confronted, Mayor Corliss admits the founding families have long known the ledger's meaning and paid to keep it quiet — but swears he never touched anyone. He gives Kestrel a key to Vane's sealed crypt. POV: Corliss then Kestrel. Emotional beat: complicity without malice; rot as tradition.

chapters.title: Inside the Crypt
chapters.summary: In the crypt, Kestrel finds Vane's true remains hidden in a side niche — moved recently — plus Merrin's working notes decoding the ledger further than Kestrel ever could. Merrin isn't hiding the secret; she's finishing it. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: dread recalibrated — the enemy is more devoted than corrupt.

chapters.title: The Keeper
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter through Merrin's perspective: orphaned, indebted, recruited years ago as the ledger's 'keeper,' she came to believe erasure was mercy and order. POV: Merrin. Emotional beat: chilling sincerity; a believer, not a monster.

chapters.title: One Name Short
chapters.summary: Merrin's notes list next targets: Ida, and Kestrel herself — scheduled for 'reinterment' after the anniversary toast. Kestrel must decide whether to flee or stand. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into choice.

chapters.title: Setting the Table
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Ida quietly prepare: copying evidence to outside authorities, arranging the hall's display cases, coaching the choir soloist who saw something nine years ago. POV: Ida. Emotional beat: quiet courage; the trap set in reverse.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Two hundred townspeople raise their glasses to Ambrose Vane. As the toast lands, Kestrel takes the stage and begins reading the decoded ledger aloud, name by paired name. Murmur becomes uproar. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: the held breath before the break.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Merrin attempts to stop her; a tense standoff in the hall ends when the choir soloist corroborates everything and deputies arrive with the evidence copies. Merrin surrenders the ledger, asking only who will keep it now. POV: Merrin then Kestrel. Emotional beat: tragic confrontation between two kinds of devotion.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: Vane is buried properly; Tobias Wrenn is buried beside his parents with the whole town attending. The founding families resign. Kestrel reads her mother's final marginal note aloud at the graveside. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: mourning completed at last.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Months later, Kestrel catalogs the cemetery anew, adding honest headstones for the erased. The ledger rests in a public exhibit, uncoded, its cipher printed on the wall. She stays. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt on truth rather than silence.
